note: KEY AND ELEMENT COERCION, the whole matrix in one value. Emacs answers (("b" . 2) nil "a" a ("a" . 1) (a . 1)). An element may be a CONS (compared by its car) or a BARE string or symbol (compared as itself), and either way the ELEMENT is what comes back, not the key and not the cdr -- s.el's `s--aget' takes the `cdr' of this. A SYMBOL on either side is coerced with `symbol-name': key `a' finds element "a", and key "a" finds a cons whose car is `a'. kg answers `void-function' at this pin. THIS CASE FLIPPED in the frontier demand phase: `assoc-string' is prelude Lisp now and answers the whole coercion matrix, the ELEMENT coming back in every shape.
